text: The moon rose round above the quiet trees.
Sunny wandered soft along the forest floor.
Between the roots she saw two shining eyes,
and a coat of chocolate brown with snow-white spots.
A little quoll, as gentle as could be,
came tiptoeing out to say a soft hello.
Her spots were like the stars up in the sky,
scattered soft and white across her back.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a starry coat!”
“The night gave me my spots,” the quoll said, smiling.
They padded down the mossy path together,
quiet as two whispers in the dark.
“I love the night,” the quoll said, soft and low.
“It's calm and cool and full of gentle stars.”
So Sunny looked up through the sleepy leaves
and saw the sky all dusted white with stars.
The little quoll grew drowsy as they walked,
her small feet slowing on the cool soft moss.
She found her den beneath a twisted root,
and curled up round just like a spotted moon.
Sunny made a bed of ferns nearby,
and nestled down beneath the starry sky.
The forest hushed. The moss was cool and soft.
Everything was peaceful, still, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy under starlit leaves.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the spotted quoll,
dreaming under stars that matched her coat.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, spotted quoll.
Goodnight, starry forest. Goodnight, little one.
